SMTO-EXE-0142 — SMTO couldn't find the app window it needed

GUID: b79e2e57-b052-5b38-b17d-458887835fba
Slug: ui-window-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO looked for the app window it was asked to work in, but found no matching window, or more than one, on that computer. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that computer), make sure the app is open and its window is not minimized. SMTO can only work in a window that currently exists on the desktop.
  2. Click the app's window once so it is the one in front, then let SMTO continue. When no exact window is named, SMTO uses the window that is in front.
  3. If the app has several similar windows open, close the ones you don't need, or tell SMTO the exact window title to use. SMTO won't guess between look-alike windows, so it needs exactly one match.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next step in the task shows it found the window and lists its buttons or fields.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the app and window, to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't let SMTO act on a different window just to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Native UI observation could not resolve one exact requested window.

What this means

  • Native window selection did not establish exactly one matching window. Some adapters classify both zero and multiple matching windows with this category. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Native window selection did not establish exactly one matching window. Some adapters classify both zero and multiple matching windows with this category.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect a fresh scoped window snapshot and narrow the exact window identity; distinguish no match from ambiguous matching.

How to fix it

  • Inspect current window metadata (desktop windows and ui.status) on the selected Gateway and pass the intended exact scope.window_id; with no window_id the adapter uses the single focused window. Narrow an ambiguous match instead of acting on an arbitrary window; macOS and Windows report both zero and multiple matches with this code.
  • Inspect current window metadata and select the intended exact window; narrow an ambiguous match rather than acting on an arbitrary window.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect ui.status and a fresh scoped ui.snapshot on the selected Gateway. Correct the target or prerequisites before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • Exactly one intended window resolves before semantic element lookup.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
